title: Your first Series and DataFrame
prompt: Build `revenue`, a Series of `values` labelled by `months`. Set `best_month` to the label of its largest value and `share` to each month's share of the yearly total (a Series that sums to 1). Then build `products`, a DataFrame with the columns `name`, `unit_price` and `unit_cost` holding the three products listed in the comments, in that order, and `margin`, a Series of `unit_price` minus `unit_cost`.
hints: `revenue.idxmax()` returns a label; dividing a Series by a single number divides every value.
Build the DataFrame from a dictionary of lists, one key per column, then subtract one column from the other: `products["unit_price"] - products["unit_cost"]`.
explanation: Passing `index=months` makes each revenue carry its month, so `idxmax()` answers "which month?" directly. `revenue / revenue.sum()` divides every value by one total: a single number combines with every element of a Series (this is called broadcasting). For the DataFrame, the dictionary keys become column names and each list becomes a column. Subtracting two columns lines them up by the shared row index, giving the skillet a margin of 21.55, the grinder 52.01 and the tent 65.91.

checks.series: `revenue` is a Series labelled Jan to Dec
checks.share: `share` sums to 1, with November at about 23%
checks.products: `products` is a 3 × 3 DataFrame with the right columns
